== con-leche/ConLeche/Model/PureChecker.lean#L30-L39
    30  /-- **Every stream the checker accepts has a model in every set theory.** -/
    31  theorem model_exists (V : Type w) [SetTheory V]
    32      (pins : List NatOpPinSet) (maxNatSize : Nat) (ds : Array Declaration)
    33      (accepted : (checkDecls .verified pins maxNatSize ds).isOk) :
    34      ∃ model, IsModel V model (· ∈ constantsOf ds.toList) := by
    35    cases h : checkDecls .verified pins maxNatSize ds with
    36    | error e => rw [h] at accepted; cases accepted
    37    | ok env =>
    38      obtain ⟨m⟩ := Cached.checkDecls_sound (V := V) h
    39      exact ⟨_, isModel_of_envModelM m (Cached.checkDecls_recordsStored h)⟩

== con-leche/ConLeche/Verify/Cached/MainC.lean#L33-L39
    33  /-- **Acceptance**: what the fold accepts carries the model. -/
    34  theorem checkDecls_sound
    35      {ds : Array Declaration} {env' : Env}
    36      (h : checkDecls .verified pins maxNatSize ds = .ok env') :
    37      Nonempty (EnvModelM V env') := by
    38    obtain ⟨n, fe, r, rfl⟩ := checkDecls_run .verified h
    39    exact (declsRun_model (V := V) r rfl ConLeche.Model.EnvModelOk.empty).nonempty

== crates/con-ron-core/src/arena/handle.rs#L4-L13
     4  //! One 32-bit word per handle, in one of two shapes.  The top bit is the tier
     5  //! in both; bit 30 says which shape the rest is:
     6  //!
     7  //! ```text
     8  //! wide   (expression `app` only)        narrow (every other node)
     9  //! bit  31      tier                     bit  31      tier
    10  //! bit  30      1                        bit  30      0
    11  //! bits 29…0    index                    bits 29…26   ctor tag   (4 bits)
    12  //!                                       bits 25…0    index
    13  //! ```

   118  /// the modes con-ron does not run are listed by name, as usage errors

   120  const HELP_TAIL: &str = "\
   121  Options:
   122    --verified          Check in the mode the soundness theorem covers (default)
   123    --trusted           Skip the checks only the proof needs; outside the theorem
   124    --jobs=N            Worker threads (default: one per hardware thread, at most 16)
   125    --max-nat-size=N    Largest Nat numeral in bytes the checker takes in or
   126                        computes; a larger one is rejected (default 134217728)
   127    --progress[=PACE]   Report progress on stderr: PACE is N declarations
   128                        (default 1), P% of each phase, or Ss seconds
   129    --pins FILE         Testing only: check with this Nat pin list instead of
   130                        the embedded one (outside the theorems)
   131    --no-pins           Testing only: check with no Nat pin list
   132    --help              Print this help and exit
   133    --                  End of options
   134  
   135  lean4export input:
   136    --compare           CHALLENGE.ndjson SOLUTION.ndjson: check SOLUTION, then
   137                        check CHALLENGE, its axioms justified by SOLUTION: each
   138                        axiom of CHALLENGE (but the standard ones) and each
   139                        declaration whose value uses sorry is accepted as an
   140                        axiom of its statement when SOLUTION holds a constant
   141                        of that name and type, up to the names of level
   142                        parameters, and everything that type reads is the same
   143                        in both, record by record. Prints the justified axioms
   144  
   145  .olean input:
   146    --olean             Read modules and their import closure from .olean files
   147    --search-path=DIRS  Colon-separated .olean directories; repeatable
   148    --constant=NAME     Check only NAME and what it mentions; repeatable
   149    --compare           CHALLENGE SOLUTION: check the closure of the module
   150                        SOLUTION, then the closure of CHALLENGE, its axioms
   151                        justified by SOLUTION's as for lean4export input.
   152                        Prints the justified axioms. With --constant=NAME
   153                        (declarations of CHALLENGE itself), only NAME and
   154                        what it reads
   155    --trusted-search-path=DIRS
   156                        With --compare: CHALLENGE and all it imports must be
   157                        in DIRS, and are read from there only; SOLUTION's
   158                        modules from DIRS first, then --search-path.
   159                        Colon-separated; repeatable
   160  
   161  con-leche's other modes, not run by con-ron yet (a usage error, exit 3):
   162    --check-graph, --module, --modular, --schedule[-OPT=V],
   163    --worker-stack-size=SIZE, and --compare with any of them
   164  
   165  Exit status:
   166    0  accepted
   167    1  rejected: a declaration is invalid
   168    2  declined: an unsupported feature
   169    3  error: bad usage, malformed input or an internal failure
   170  
   171  Documentation:
   172    README.md and OVERVIEW.md of the con-ron repository";

== crates/con-ron/src/driver.rs#L18-L23
    18  //! | exit | verdict | meaning |
    19  //! |---|---|---|
    20  //! | 0 | `accepted N declarations` | every declaration checked; `N` counts the file's declaration records |
    21  //! | 1 | `rejected` | a declaration is invalid |
    22  //! | 2 | `declined` | the checker positively detected a feature it does not support, and says which |

   620  pub fn render(n: &Name) -> Vec<u32> {
   621      match &n.0.kind {
   622          NameKind::Anonymous => {
   623              const A: [u32; 11] = [91, 97, 110, 111, 110, 121, 109, 111, 117, 115, 93];
   624              crate::kernel::core_types::code_points(&A)
   625          }
   626          _ => {
   627              let cs = component_list(n, Vec::new());
   628              let k = cs.len();
   629              display_acc_finish(render_from(&cs, k, display_acc_empty()))
   630          }
   631      }
   632  }

== proof/ConRon/Capstone.lean#L18-L92
    18  /-!
    19  # `ConRon.Capstone` — THE COMPOSITION: Theorem 2 ∘ Theorem 1 ∘ con-leche
    20  
    21  DESIGN.md §8.2's last line: *"Capstones for the binary = Theorem 2 ∘
    22  Theorem 1 ∘ con-leche."*  This is the one module that imports both
    23  `ConRon.Bridge` (Theorem 1, (B) ⇒ (A)) and `ConRon.Refine2` (Theorem 2,
    24  (C) ⇒ (B)), and it states the binary's headline theorems:
    25  
    26  * `ConRon.Capstone.model_exists` — the environment of every stream the Aeneas
    27    model of the Rust pipeline accepts has a model in every set theory;
    28  * `ConRon.Capstone.no_False_declaration` — a file that declares a theorem of
    29    type `False` is never accepted by it;
    30  * `no_False_oleans` / `model_exists_oleans` — the same on `--olean`;
    31  * `model_exists_compare` / `no_False_compare` and `model_exists_oleans_compare` /
    32    `no_False_oleans_compare` — the same for a challenge checked with its axioms justified by
    33    a solution (`--compare`, §4b and §4c), about the challenge alone.
    34  
    35  **They are the campaign's root theorems** (task #97-COMPOSE): the sorry
    36  frontier is measured as their dependency closure, and §5's census prints their
    37  axioms.  What they assume is exactly their premises, listed below.
    38  
    39  ## The pipeline, stage by stage
    40  
    41  The binary (`crates/con-ron/src/bin/con-ron.rs`) is an unverified driver
    42  around the extracted core functions and the pin decoder, in this order, on
    43  one `AState` made from `EStore::empty()` and one `PersTier::empty()`:
    44  
    45      intern_reserved_pins → builtin_prelude_e → parse_source
    46        → prepare_d → (decode) → intern_all_pins → (the check phase)
    47  
    48  **The check phase is the one the binary's driver runs, pool and all**
    49  (`driver::check_decls_driver`): it builds the stream's index from the records
    50  (`stream_index::build_index`), freezes the tier with the index in it
    51  (`checker::freeze_tier`), runs every record's job on `pool::parallel_all`, and
    52  thaws the tier.  The headlines take one premise per step (`h6` the index, `h7`
    53  the freeze, `h8` the pool), which `poolAccepts_intro` assembles into
    54  `Refine2/Checker/Phased.lean`'s `PoolAccepts`.  `h8` is the contract of the generic
    55  combinator `pool::parallel_all` at the driver's two verified closures (`ParallelAll`
    56  at `jobStep`): index lists, one per worker, covering every job, each in increasing
    57  order, and for each a fold of `run_job` over its indices from `worker_state`,
    58  accepting.  That contract is the pool's trusted claim (OVERVIEW §8.2): control flow of
    59  `pool.rs`, nothing about the checker.
    60  
    61  The proof:
    62  
    63  1. **Theorem 2, per stage** — `Refine2`'s `…_refines` lemmas walk the Rust runs
    64     into twin runs from the twin's own start state `AState.init EStore.empty`,
    65     related at every step (`AStateRel₀`/`AStateInv`: lockstep); `rust_stages`;
    66  2. **Theorem 1** — `Bridge/Stages.lean` takes the twin runs:
    67     `Arena.pooledAccepts_bridge` makes the check phase's accept con-leche's pure
    68     fold `checkDeclsPure` accepting the denoted stream at `streamEnv` of it;
    69  3. **con-leche** — `checkDeclsPure_sound_of` turns the pure accept into a model,
    70     and `no_proof_of_False_pure` refutes a `False` theorem in the stream.
    71  
    72  ## The named hypotheses
    73  
    74  The headlines start from the binary's own start values (`startState` =
    75  `AState::empty()`, `emptyTier` = `PersTier::empty()`) and name the call the
    76  binary makes at each step.  Beside `[ConLeche.SetTheory V]`, the file's shape
    77  `hfalse` and the one premise per call (`h1`…`h5`, `hpins`, `h6`…`h8`), what
    78  they assume is exactly:
    79  
    80  * `hreads : ReadsAs sinst src chunks.val` — the reads are the chunks: the binary
    81    parses with the verified reader loop `parse_source` over the driver's file
    82    handle, and `Refine2/Frontend/Source.lean`'s `parse_source_eq` makes that
    83    `parse_chunks` over the chunks the handle hands out; that the handle hands out
    84    the file's bytes, in order, is the input seam;
    85  * on `--olean`, `hsnap : SnapshotOf finst fsv F` — the file instance answers as
    86    one snapshot `F`.
    87  
    88  `hpins` is the premise for the binary's pin step: the pin list is what the verified
    89  decoder read, at any text (as con-leche's theorems hold at every pin list);
    90  `model_exists_embedded` / `no_False_declaration_embedded` fix the text to the embedded
    91  `PINS_TEXT`.
    92  -/

== proof/ConRon/Refine2/Frontend/Source.lean#L34-L38
    34  def ReadsAs {S : Type} (inst : frontend.export_c.ChunkSource S) :
    35      S → List (alloc.vec.Vec Std.U8) → Prop
    36    | src, [] => ∃ e src', inst.next_chunk src = ok (e, src') ∧ e.val = []
    37    | src, c :: cs => c.val ≠ [] ∧
    38        ∃ src', inst.next_chunk src = ok (c, src') ∧ ReadsAs inst src' cs

== proof/ConRon/Capstone.lean#L193-L206
   193  structure SnapshotOf {Fs : Type} (inst : frontend.olean.files.OleanFs Fs) (fsv : Fs)
   194      (F : ConLeche.FS) : Prop where
   195    path_exists : ∀ {p q}, PathRel p q → ∀ b, inst.path_exists fsv p = ok (.Ok b) →
   196      b = (F.real q).isSome
   197    is_dir : ∀ {p q}, PathRel p q → ∀ b, inst.is_dir fsv p = ok (.Ok b) → b = F.dir q
   198    real_path : ∀ {p q}, PathRel p q → ∀ r, inst.real_path fsv p = ok (.Ok r) →
   199      F.real q = some ⟨ConRon.Refine.absString r⟩ ∧ ConRon.Refine.StrWF r
   200    read_bin_file : ∀ {p q}, PathRel p q → ∀ b, inst.read_bin_file fsv p = ok (.Ok b) →
   201      F.file q = some (absBytes (alloc.vec.Vec.deref b))
   202    read_range : ∀ {p q}, PathRel p q → ∀ off len b, inst.read_range fsv p off len = ok (.Ok b) →
   203      ∃ whole, F.file q = some whole ∧ absBytes (alloc.vec.Vec.deref b) =
   204        whole.extract off.val (min (off.val + len.val) whole.size)
   205    file_size : ∀ {p q}, PathRel p q → ∀ s, inst.file_size fsv p = ok (.Ok s) →
   206      ∃ whole, F.file q = some whole ∧ s.val = whole.size

    69  @[expose] def MixedStep (pinsP : List NatOpPinSet) (JS : Solution) (env : Env) (pd : Declaration)
    70      (env' : Env) : Prop :=
    71    (justifiable pd = none ∧
    72      ∃ F, ConLeche.checkDecl .verified (fueledOps .verified F) pinsP env pd = .ok env') ∨
    73    (∃ cv, justifiable pd = some cv ∧ env' = ⟨.axiomInfo cv :: env.consts, env.tables⟩ ∧
    74      justifyWhy JS (mkFEnv env) cv = none ∧ basisNamesOk pd = true ∧
    75      ∃ F, ConstantValRun F env cv cv.type)

== crates/con-ron-core/src/arena/handle.rs#L4-L30
     4  //! One 32-bit word per handle, in one of two shapes.  The top bit is the tier
     5  //! in both; bit 30 says which shape the rest is:
     6  //!
     7  //! ```text
     8  //! wide   (expression `app` only)        narrow (every other node)
     9  //! bit  31      tier                     bit  31      tier
    10  //! bit  30      1                        bit  30      0
    11  //! bits 29…0    index                    bits 29…26   ctor tag   (4 bits)
    12  //!                                       bits 25…0    index
    13  //! ```
    14  //!
    15  //! (tier 0 = persistent, 1 = scratch; the index is into THAT CONSTRUCTOR'S
    16  //! array of THAT TIER).  The zero word is a narrow handle — tag 0,
    17  //! persistent, slot 0 — which is the twin's `default : Idx k` and every
    18  //! `of_word(0)` below: the anonymous name, the level `zero`, a handle that
    19  //! decodes.  An expression `app` array holds 2^30 = 1 073 741 824 nodes per
    20  //! tier and every other constructor array 2^26 =
    21  //! 67 108 864: apps are 85 % of an export's expression nodes, so they are the
    22  //! array that runs out first, and they get the room.  Only the expression
    23  //! `app` tag is wide — a level `param` handle is narrow although `LTAG_PARAM`
    24  //! has `ETAG_APP`'s value — and `word_tag` reads `ETAG_APP` off a word with
    25  //! bit 30 set, so the tag of a handle is read the same way for all four
    26  //! kinds.
    27  //!
    28  //! The tier is the TOP bit, above both shapes' index, so a persistent
    29  //! handle's bits never change when the scratch tier comes and goes
    30  //! (con-leche's lesson 6).

== crates/con-ron-core/src/arena/store.rs#L3623-L3658
  3623  
  3624      /// con-leche: none — arena infrastructure; Lean twin: proof/ConRon/Arena/Store.lean:482-502 EStore.intern
  3625      /// Hash-cons an expression node: probe the persistent cons table, then the
  3626      /// scratch one, then append to the tier the store is in (DESIGN.md §8.3).
  3627      /// The cap test is the Lean's `capOK` turned into the `Native` decline
  3628      /// §8.3 puts here.
  3629      ///
  3630      /// **Dispatched ONCE** (task #97-P6-15).  The body below used to run the
  3631      /// whole sequence over the `ENodeView`, and each of its four steps
  3632      /// dispatched on the view's tag again and built the node record again:
  3633      /// the persistent probe built it (inside `ETables::find`), the scratch
  3634      /// probe built it a second time, `der_of_view` re-dispatched to compute
  3635      /// the derived word, and `ETables::push` re-dispatched and built it a
  3636      /// third time to append it.  So the tag is read once here and the ten per-constructor
  3637      /// paths below each build their record ONCE and hand the same `&r` to the
  3638      /// two probes, to the capacity test and to the push — the same clauses in
  3639      /// the same order, with the dispatch and the two rebuilds gone.
  3640      ///
  3641      /// The twin's `intern` is one `def` over `ENodeView`; what is owed is the
  3642      /// ten-arm spelling and `internC v = intern (view of C)` per constructor,
  3643      /// each of them `rfl` after the `match`.
  3644      pub fn intern(&mut self, pers: &PersTier, v: ENodeView) -> Result<EIdx, CheckError> {
  3645          match v {
  3646              ENodeView::BVar(i) => self.intern_bvar(pers, i),
  3647              ENodeView::FVar(idx, ty) => self.intern_fvar(pers, idx, ty),
  3648              ENodeView::Sort(u) => self.intern_sort(pers, u),
  3649              ENodeView::Const(n, us) => self.intern_const(pers, n, us),
  3650              ENodeView::App(f, a) => self.intern_app(pers, f, a),
  3651              ENodeView::Lam(ty, body) => self.intern_lam(pers, ty, body),
  3652              ENodeView::ForallE(ty, body) => self.intern_forall_e(pers, ty, body),
  3653              ENodeView::LetE(ty, val, body) => self.intern_let_e(pers, ty, val, body),
  3654              ENodeView::Lit(l) => self.intern_lit(pers, l),
  3655              ENodeView::Proj(n, i, e) => self.intern_proj(pers, n, i, e),
  3656          }
  3657      }
  3658  

== crates/con-ron-core/src/arena/store.rs#L3908-L3955
  3908      pub fn intern_app(&mut self, pers: &PersTier, f: EIdx, a: EIdx) -> Result<EIdx, CheckError> {
  3909          let r: AppNode = AppNode { f, a };
  3910          let sk: bool = if self.scratch_on {
  3911              if r.f.is_persistent() {
  3912                  !r.a.is_persistent()
  3913              } else {
  3914                  true
  3915              }
  3916          } else {
  3917              false
  3918          };
  3919          let hit: Option<EIdx> = if sk {
  3920              None
  3921          } else if pers.frozen {
  3922              pers.e.apps.find(&r)
  3923          } else {
  3924              self.pers.apps.find(&r)
  3925          };
  3926          match hit {
  3927              Some(hp) => Ok(hp),
  3928              None => {
  3929                  if self.scratch_on {
  3930                      let at: (usize, Option<EIdx>) = self.scr.apps.find_slot(&r);
  3931                      match at.1 {
  3932                          Some(hs) => Ok(hs),
  3933                          None => {
  3934                              if self.scr.apps.full_wide() {
  3935                                  Err(CheckError::Native(code_points(&M_E_CAP)))
  3936                              } else {
  3937                                  let d: u64 = self.der_of_app(pers, &r.f, &r.a);
  3938                                  let h: EIdx =
  3939                                      EIdx::pack_wide(TIER_S, self.scr.apps.size() as u32);
  3940                                  self.scr.apps.push_at(at.0, r, d, h.dup2());
  3941                                  Ok(h)
  3942                              }
  3943                          }
  3944                      }
  3945                  } else if self.pers.apps.full_wide() {
  3946                      Err(CheckError::Native(code_points(&M_E_CAP)))
  3947                  } else {
  3948                      let d: u64 = self.der_of_app(pers, &r.f, &r.a);
  3949                      let h: EIdx = EIdx::pack_wide(TIER_P, self.pers.apps.size() as u32);
  3950                      self.pers.apps.push(r, d, h.dup2());
  3951                      Ok(h)
  3952                  }
  3953              }
  3954          }
  3955      }

== crates/con-ron-core/src/arena/core.rs#L12051-L12070
 12051  /// con-leche: none — **a job's bracket, closed** (DESIGN.md §8.3)
 12052  /// Lean twin: `proof/ConRon/Arena/Core.lean:4578-4586 dropScratch` —
 12053  /// the twin's `dropScratch` on a store that STAYS frozen (task #98-FREEZE): the
 12054  /// caches flushed and the scratch tiers emptied, the flag untouched.  A
 12055  /// worker's store is frozen for its whole life, so between two jobs it is
 12056  /// frozen with an empty scratch tier where the twin's is scratch-off; nothing
 12057  /// is interned there.
 12058  pub fn leave_record(st: &mut AState) {
 12059      flush_caches(st);
 12060      st.store.clear_scratch();
 12061  }
 12062  
 12063  /// con-leche: none — **a job's bracket, opened** (DESIGN.md §8.3)
 12064  /// Lean twin: `proof/ConRon/Arena/Core.lean:4588-4595 enterScratch` —
 12065  /// the twin's `enterScratch` on an already frozen store (task #98-FREEZE): the
 12066  /// memos cleared and the scratch tiers emptied, the flag untouched.
 12067  pub fn enter_record(st: &mut AState) {
 12068      st.memos.reset();
 12069      st.store.clear_scratch();
 12070  }

== crates/con-ron-core/src/arena/checker.rs#L65-L88
    65  
    66  /// con-leche: none — the phase boundary, which con-leche has no tier to make
    67  /// Lean twin: none — the twin has no tier to move; its worker reads the
    68  /// persistent tier where it is (`AState.worker`, `Arena/Checker.lean`).
    69  /// **The persistent tier and the stream's index into a value**: the four
    70  /// persistent tables and the index move into one `PersTier` handed back
    71  /// `frozen`, for the workers to read (the index is the base `ifenv_find` reads
    72  /// below a job's own layer).  A pure MOVE: the store's scratch tiers and flags
    73  /// are untouched (a worker's store is its own, `worker_state`), and
    74  /// `thaw_tier` puts everything back where it was.  The driver's store is not
    75  /// read between the two.
    76  pub fn freeze_tier(ar: &mut EStore, ix: IStreamIndex) -> PersTier {
    77      let n: NTables = core::mem::replace(&mut ar.lss.ls.ns.pers, NTables::empty());
    78      let l: LTables = core::mem::replace(&mut ar.lss.ls.pers, LTables::empty());
    79      let ls: LsTables = core::mem::replace(&mut ar.lss.pers, LsTables::empty());
    80      let e: ETables = core::mem::replace(&mut ar.pers, ETables::empty());
    81      PersTier {
    82          frozen: true,
    83          n,
    84          l,
    85          ls,
    86          e,
    87          env: ix,
    88      }

== crates/con-ron-core/src/arena/store.rs#L1229-L1281
  1229  /// con-leche: none — arena infrastructure; Lean twin: proof/ConRon/Arena/Store.lean:365-373 EStore
  1230  /// **The persistent tier of all four stores, as one value `n` phase-B workers
  1231  /// read by reference** — DESIGN.md §8.3's "the persistent tier is immutable in
  1232  /// phase B, each worker owns a scratch tier — no atomics anywhere", made
  1233  /// expressible.
  1234  ///
  1235  /// Each store keeps its own `pers` field, which is the tier the PARSE and
  1236  /// phase A's setup append to, and ONE flag, `scratch_on`.  **A store is in
  1237  /// one of two states, and "frozen" and "scratch on" are the same thing** (task
  1238  /// #98-FREEZE):
  1239  ///
  1240  /// * **owned, scratch off** (the parse, the setup, between phase A's
  1241  ///   declaration brackets): read through the EMPTY stand-in tier
  1242  ///   (`PersTier::empty`, `frozen` false), so every persistent read and every
  1243  ///   append goes to the owned field;
  1244  /// * **frozen, scratch on** (inside a declaration bracket, and a phase-B
  1245  ///   worker for its whole life): the owned field is empty — `freeze` moved it
  1246  ///   into a `PersTier` whose `frozen` bit is set — and the store is read
  1247  ///   through that tier, so every persistent read goes to it; every append is
  1248  ///   a SCRATCH append, so no append can reach a frozen persistent tier, by
  1249  ///   construction and not by a guard.
  1250  ///
  1251  /// Which tables a persistent read goes to is therefore the READER's to say
  1252  /// (`frozen`), not the store's: the choice is made by a value that is fixed
  1253  /// for the whole of a bracket or a worker, whatever runs inside it.  `freeze`
  1254  /// hands out a frozen tier and turns the scratch tier on; `thaw` takes it back
  1255  /// and turns it off; `empty_frozen` is a worker's store.  Promotion — the one
  1256  /// writer of the persistent tier inside a bracket — writes the frozen tier
  1257  /// itself, through `&mut PersTier` (`PersTier::intern_*`).
  1258  ///
  1259  /// **Why a shared PARAMETER and not a field of the state.**  Task #97-P6-6
  1260  /// measured a region inside the threaded `&mut` state eight ways: a bare
  1261  /// `&u64` field on `AState` costs five function bodies Aeneas cannot
  1262  /// translate and the same borrow inside the four stores costs sixteen, while
  1263  /// everything else this split needs — the two-tier layout, the flag, the
  1264  /// value-returning readers below — extracts at zero errors.  So the sharing
  1265  /// arrives as an ordinary shared parameter, the shape `fe: &IFEnv` and `mode:
  1266  /// &CheckMode` already have, and the twin's monad becomes `ReaderT PersTier
  1267  /// (StateT AState (Except CheckError))`.
  1268  pub struct PersTier {
  1269      /// This is a frozen store's tier: a store read through it reads its
  1270      /// persistent tables HERE.  `false` only for the empty stand-in an owned
  1271      /// store is handed (`PersTier::empty`), which is never read.
  1272      pub frozen: bool,
  1273      pub n: NTables,
  1274      pub l: LTables,
  1275      pub ls: LsTables,
  1276      pub e: ETables,
  1277      /// The stream's index, the frozen base of every job's environment
  1278      /// (`arena::env`'s `IFEnv` note): `checker::freeze_tier` moves it here, so
  1279      /// every worker reads one by reference.  Empty in every other tier.
  1280      pub env: IStreamIndex,
  1281  }

   749  /// con-leche: ConLeche/Kernel/FEnv.lean:189-218 FEnv
   750  /// Lean twin: `proof/ConRon/Arena/Env.lean:274-286 IFEnv` — the environment
   751  /// with its `O(1)` index (DESIGN.md §8.3 lesson 13), over the frozen base of a
   752  /// stream's index, and the two literal flags of its lookups.  con-leche's `ovl`
   753  /// field is not ported (see `ifenv_find`).
   754  ///
   755  /// **The environment has two tiers, like the store.**  An `IFEnv` is one LAYER:
   756  /// a job's own, empty until its record pushes.  The BASE is the stream's index
   757  /// (`arena::stream_index::IStreamIndex`), built once before any check and

   760  /// index has no counter); the base is read below the layer's two bounds,

   762  /// base itself is shared.
   763  ///

   765  /// lever 1): the twin's row carries the constant itself, a shared value in Lean
   766  /// and a second deep copy in Rust.  Every writer keeps `idx` and `env.consts`
   767  /// in step (`ifenv_push`, `ifenv_push_temp`, `ifenv_pop_temp`) and
   768  /// `ifenv_find` reads `env.consts[s]`.  The table map `tbls` is built the same
   769  /// way: its row is the table's slot in `env.tables`.

   780      /// reads it at every literal it meets, so it is set where the layer is made
   781      /// and kept by every push.
   782      pub nat_lit: bool,
   783      /// **Are string literals expandable** here (`str_lit_stored_by`), as
   784      /// `nat_lit`.
   785      pub str_lit: bool,
   786  }

== crates/con-ron-core/src/arena/core_state.rs#L466-L513
   466  /// con-leche: none — arena infrastructure (task #97-PERF-WALKMEMO)
   467  /// The slot count past which `take_walk_memo` hands back a FRESH table
   468  /// instead of a cleared one; see its note for how the value was chosen.
   469  pub const WALK_MEMO_KEEP: usize = 1 << 16;
   470  
   471  /// con-leche: ConLeche/Cached/ExprOpsC.lean:2409-2413 allLevelParamsDefinedC
   472  /// con-leche: ConLeche/Cached/StateC.lean:666-668 constsResolveFC
   473  /// Lean twin: the `∅` that `proof/ConRon/Arena/CheckerBase.lean`'s
   474  /// `allLevelParamsDefined` and `constsResolveFFast` start their walk from —
   475  /// **the parked walk memo, moved out of the state and emptied** (task
   476  /// #97-PERF-WALKMEMO).  The slot is left holding `HashMap::new()` (which
   477  /// allocates nothing) for the length of the walk, and the entry puts the
   478  /// grown table back afterwards; either way the table this returns is empty,
   479  /// so the walk starts where the twin's does.
   480  ///
   481  /// **nanoda's guard** (`nanoda_lib/src/expr.rs`, `inst`): a table past
   482  /// `WALK_MEMO_KEEP` slots is dropped rather than kept, so that one huge walk
   483  /// does not leave a huge table behind for every later call.  `reset_map`'s
   484  /// `clear_fit` already decays such a table, one eighth of its high-water mark
   485  /// a call, so the guard only decides which of the two is cheaper for an
   486  /// outlier: re-growing from nothing, or `clear_fit`'s re-make at the decayed
   487  /// size.  The threshold, measured on `Init` (`--verified --jobs=1`, one
   488  /// `perf stat -e instructions:u` run each, all accepting 57 977):
   489  ///
   490  /// | `WALK_MEMO_KEEP` | instructions:u |
   491  /// |---|---:|
   492  /// | fresh `HashMap::new()` per call (before) | 211 976 016 505 |
   493  /// | 2^10 slots (nanoda's 1024) | 208 379 555 799 |
   494  /// | 2^12 | 206 572 063 910 |
   495  /// | 2^14 | 205 851 105 938 |
   496  /// | **2^16** | **205 785 515 243** |
   497  /// | no guard (2^60) | 205 783 023 575 |
   498  ///
   499  /// A guard low enough to trip on ordinary calls gives the saving back — at
   500  /// nanoda's 1024 more than half of it — because those calls re-grow by
   501  /// doubling, which is exactly the cost this table exists to avoid.  2^16 is
   502  /// the smallest power tried that costs nothing measurable on `Init` (2.5 M
   503  /// instructions over no guard), so it only ever fires on an outlier.
   504  pub fn take_walk_memo<K, V>(slot: &mut HashMap<K, V>) -> HashMap<K, V> {
   505      let m: HashMap<K, V> = core::mem::replace(slot, HashMap::new());
   506      if m.capacity() > WALK_MEMO_KEEP {
   507          HashMap::new()
   508      } else {
   509          let mut m2: HashMap<K, V> = m;
   510          reset_map(&mut m2);
   511          m2
   512      }
   513  }

== crates/con-ron-core/src/ron/hashmap2.rs#L1-L40
     1  //! con-leche: none — arena infrastructure; a second `Std.HashMap` replacement, proved
     2  //!
     3  //! `ron::HashMap2<K, V>` — proved in `proof/ConRon/Refine/HashMap2.lean`
     4  //! (task #97-HM2; designed in task #97-P6-4b).  The same abstract object as
     5  //! `ron::hashmap`'s `HashMap` — a partial map from `K` to `V`, with
     6  //! `Hashable`/`Eq2`/`Dup` as its dictionaries and the same eleven operations
     7  //! — over an **open-addressed, epoch-stamped, flat slot vector** instead of
     8  //! the Aeneas tutorial's chained buckets.  `ron::hashmap` is untouched and
     9  //! keeps its proofs (`proof/ConRon/Refine/HashMap.lean`); this module's are
    10  //! in `proof/ConRon/Refine/HashMap2.lean` (task #97-HM2).
    11  //!
    12  //! **Why it exists.**  Task #97-P6-1 left `clear_slots + allocate_slots +
    13  //! move_elements*` at 21.8 % of `Init`, "all halving recursions over chained
    14  //! buckets".  Task #97-P6-4b counted what those recursions actually do on
    15  //! `Init`, and the counts name the representation rather than the code:
    16  //!
    17  //! | on `Init`, `ron::HashMap` | count |
    18  //! |---|---:|
    19  //! | `get` calls | 1 228 953 968 |
    20  //! | — resolved in 0 or 1 chain step | 98.8 % |
    21  //! | `insert` calls | 627 320 951 |
    22  //! | **`clear` calls** | **36 053 620** |
    23  //! | **— buckets walked by them** | **2 940 488 064** |
    24  //! | — entries those buckets held | 586 917 896 |
    25  //! | buckets pushed by `allocate_slots` | 948 184 512 |
    26  //! | entries moved by `move_elements*` | 349 323 629 |
    27  //!
    28  //! So the chains are *already* short — the table is a good hash table — and
    29  //! essentially all of the 21.8 % is the per-bucket cost of **emptying and
    30  //! re-growing** the slot vector: 2.94 G bucket writes to clear 0.59 G entries
    31  //! (five buckets walked per entry cleared; the average cleared table is 82
    32  //! buckets holding 16 entries) and 0.95 G `Vec::push`es to allocate them back.
    33  //! Nothing a better chain walk can do touches that.
    34  //!
    35  //! **The representation.**
    36  //!
    37  //! * `slots : Vec<Slot<K, V>>`, `Slot` = `Vacant | Live(u32, K, V)`.  No
    38  //!   `Box`, no chain, no allocation per entry — an entry *is* a slot.
    39  //! * A `Live` slot is **live only if its stamp is the table's `epoch`**;
    40  //!   a `Live` slot with a stale stamp is free space, indistinguishable from

== crates/con-ron/src/bin/con-ron.rs#L435-L667
   435  /// reject and the internal error of the two frontend gates and of the
   436  /// preparation (con-leche writes the three arms out at each gate).
   437  fn frontend_exit(e: &CheckError, mode_tag: &str) -> u8 {
   438      match classify(e) {
   439          FrontendClass::Declined(what) => {
   440              eprintln!("con-ron: declined: {} ({})", what, mode_tag);
   441              2
   442          }
   443          FrontendClass::Invalid(what) => {
   444              eprintln!("con-ron: invalid: {} ({})", what, mode_tag);
   445              1
   446          }
   447          FrontendClass::Internal(msg) => {
   448              eprintln!("con-ron: {} ({})", msg, mode_tag);
   449              3
   450          }
   451      }
   452  }

   454  /// con-leche: ConLeche/Driver/CheckMain.lean:55-62 Input
   455  /// **What a run reads**: a lean4export stream, or the import closure of root
   456  /// modules read from their `.olean` files along a search path.
   457  enum Input {
   458      Ndjson(String),
   459      Oleans(con_ron::olean_fs::OleanRequest),
   460  }
   461  
   462  /// con-leche: ConLeche/Driver/Dispatch.lean:26-62 Req
   463  /// **What a run is**: a check of one input (`check_main`), or a compared run of
   464  /// two lean4export files or two modules (`con_ron::compare`).
   465  enum Run {
   466      Check(Input),
   467      CompareJson(String, String),
   468      CompareOleans(con_ron::compare::CmpRequest),
   469  }
   470  
   471  /// con-leche: ConLeche/Driver/CheckMain.lean:233-385 checkMainG
   472  /// con-leche: ConLeche/Driver/CheckMain.lean:87-98 readInputG
   473  /// The driver's front matter: the prelude, the streaming parse, the
   474  /// preparation, the pin walk, the receipts, then the index, the check phase
   475  /// and the verdict.
   476  /// It is the Lean twin's `runPipelineIO` with the heartbeat and the receipts
   477  /// around it (`Arena/Main.lean`), and `con-ron`'s `check_main` with the
   478  /// handles in place of the trees.
   479  fn check_main(a: &Args, input: &Input) -> u8 {
   480      let t0 = Instant::now();
   481      let mode_tag = if a.verified {
   482          "--verified"
   483      } else {
   484          "--trusted"
   485      };
   486      let mode = if a.verified {
   487          CheckMode::Verified
   488      } else {
   489          CheckMode::Trusted
   490      };
   491      // ONE store for the whole run: the prelude, the stream and the pins are
   492      // hash-consed together into its persistent tier (DESIGN.md §8.3).
   493      // ConRon.Capstone: `startState`
   494      let mut st = AState::empty();
   495      // THE PERSISTENT TIER a worker reads (DESIGN.md §8.3, task #97-P6-6b).
   496      // The parse, the pin walk and the index build own their own — the store is
   497      // owned (not frozen) — so what they are handed here is the EMPTY tier; the
   498      // check phase freezes the store's tier, the index with it, into a
   499      // `PersTier` and hands `&` it to every worker (`check_decls_driver`).
   500      // ConRon.Capstone: `emptyTier`
   501      let pers: &PersTier = &PersTier::empty();
   502      // THE RESERVED-NAME PINS, interned once into that persistent tier before
   503      // anything else touches it (task #97-P6-4a, `arena::pins`): the scratch
   504      // tier is closed here, so every pinned handle is persistent and survives
   505      // every job's bracket.  Until this has run, every `pin_*`
   506      // read raises `Internal` rather than answering — which is what makes the
   507      // initialisation-order hazard task #97c named impossible rather than
   508      // unlikely.
   509      // ConRon.Capstone: h1
   510      match con_ron_core::arena::pins::intern_reserved_pins(pers, &mut st) {
   511          Ok(()) => (),
   512          Err(e) => {
   513              eprintln!(
   514                  "con-ron: the reserved-name pins do not intern ({}) ({})",
   515                  con_ron::driver::message(&e),
   516                  mode_tag
   517              );
   518              return 3;
   519          }
   520      }
   521      // The heartbeat (`--progress`), and its first line: what the run reads.
   522      let mut hb = Heartbeat::new(con_ron_core::frontend::pace::pace_dup(&a.progress), t0);
   523      hb.read_starts(&match input {
   524          Input::Ndjson(file) => con_ron::render::display_path(file),
   525          Input::Oleans(req) => req.label(pers, &st),
   526      });
   527      // THE BUILT-IN PRELUDE, parsed into that store before anything else.
   528      // ConRon.Capstone: h2
   529      let prelude_ix = match prelude::builtin_prelude_e(pers, &mut st) {
   530          Ok(p) => p,
   531          Err((e, line)) => {
   532              let what = match classify(&e) {
   533                  FrontendClass::Internal(m) => format!("does not parse (line {}: {})", line, m),
   534                  FrontendClass::Declined(w) => format!("is unsupported ({})", w),
   535                  FrontendClass::Invalid(w) => format!("contradicts itself ({})", w),
   536              };
   537              eprintln!(
   538                  "con-ron: the built-in prelude {}; regenerate it with \
   539                   `lake exe natop-pins-export` ({})",
   540                  what, mode_tag
   541              );
   542              return 3;
   543          }
   544      };
   545      // Streaming frontend: the file is read 4 MiB at a time and each buffer is
   546      // parsed and dropped, so neither a wholesale text buffer nor a scratch
   547      // file exists.  What comes out is the FILE's records as HANDLES into the
   548      // store above.  No model is ever read from the input: every inductive
   549      // block — mutual and nested included — installs through the kernel's
   550      // uniform installer, unconditionally (task #105).
   551      // ConRon.Capstone: hreads, h3 (`parse_source` over the file's handle)
   552      // The `.olean` path ends in the same records (task #142); no capstone
   553      // premise is about it yet (OVERVIEW.md).
   554      // An `--olean` run's theorems hold references to their values, which their
   555      // jobs read (`driver::olean_job`); what that needs comes back beside the
   556      // records (`OleanRead`), and of it the check keeps only the pins and the
   557      // values (below, after the preparation).
   558      let read: std::io::Result<Result<(Vec<IDeclaration>, Option<OleanRead>), (CheckError, u64)>> = match input {
   559          Input::Ndjson(file) => match driver::parse_export_stream_d(pers, &mut st, file, export_c::CHUNK_SIZE) {
   560              Err(e) => {
   561                  eprintln!("con-ron: {}: {}", con_ron::render::display_path(file), e);
   562                  return 3;
   563              }
   564              Ok((r, _)) => Ok(r.map(|p: ParseResultD| (p.decls, None))),
   565          },
   566          Input::Oleans(req) => Ok(con_ron::olean_fs::read_request(pers, &mut st, req, &a.progress)
   567              .map(|mut rd| (std::mem::take(&mut rd.decls), Some(rd)))),
   568      };
   569      let label: String = match input {
   570          Input::Ndjson(file) => con_ron::render::display_path(file),
   571          Input::Oleans(req) => req.label(pers, &st),
   572      };
   573      let (parsed_decls, olean): (Vec<IDeclaration>, Option<OleanRead>) = match read {
   574          Err(_) => return 3,
   575          Ok(Err((e, line))) => match classify(&e) {
   576              FrontendClass::Declined(what) => {
   577                  eprintln!("con-ron: declined: {} ({})", what, mode_tag);
   578                  return 2;
   579              }
   580              // A stream whose inductive block contradicts its own declarations
   581              // in a REDUNDANT field is rejected at the parse.
   582              FrontendClass::Invalid(what) => {
   583                  eprintln!("con-ron: invalid: {} ({})", what, mode_tag);
   584                  return 1;
   585              }
   586              FrontendClass::Internal(msg) => {
   587                  eprintln!("con-ron: {}:{}: {}", label, line, msg);
   588                  return 3;
   589              }
   590          },
   591          Ok(Ok(r)) => r,
   592      };
   593      let file_records = parsed_decls.len();
   594      // From here on the store is the checker's state: the memo tables and the
   595      // per-declaration caches join it (`AState`), and every handle the parse
   596      // produced indexes into it.
   597      // **PREPARE** (`frontend::prepare`): what the fold runs over is
   598      // `prepare_prelude` of the file's records — the prelude's declarations
   599      // first (the stream's own copies where it has them, the rest synthesised),
   600      // then the stream's, with every pinned `Nat` operation's stream-certified
   601      // ground hoisted ahead of it.  It takes the whole state since task
   602      // #97-P4d: step 2 is the real ground hoist, which interns.
   603      // ConRon.Capstone: h4
   604      // What a record mentions, for the ground hoist: its expressions say it,
   605      // except a theorem's read from an `.olean`, whose load read it off the
   606      // file (con-leche's `usedOf`).
   607      let prepared = match match &olean {
   608          None => prepare::prepare_d(pers, &mut st, prelude_ix, parsed_decls, &DeclUsedConsts),
   609          Some(rd) => prepare::prepare_d(pers, &mut st, prelude_ix, parsed_decls, rd),
   610      } {
   611          Ok(p) => p,
   612          Err(e) => return frontend_exit(&e, mode_tag),
   613      };
   614      // **What the check keeps of the read** (con-leche's `checkOleansG` takes
   615      // `rd.values`): the reader's pins and the values' modules.  The merged
   616      // constants, whose last reader is the preparation (`OleanRead.thmUses`), go
   617      // here, before the pool: on Mathlib that is 0.8 M constants and their
   618      // `uses` (DESIGN, task #145).
   619      let olean: Option<(OleanPins, Vec<ModRef>)> =
   620          olean.map(|rd| (rd.pins, rd.values));
   621      // the ground hoist's receipt
   622      if !prepared.hoisted.is_empty() {
   623          let names: Vec<String> = prepared
   624              .hoisted
   625              .iter()
   626              .map(|n| driver::name_of(pers, &st.store, n))
   627              .collect();
   628          eprintln!(
   629              "con-ron: {} declarations hoisted ahead of the pinned Nat operations \
   630               they ground: {}",
   631              prepared.hoisted.len(),
   632              names.join(", ")
   633          );
   634      }
   635      // ConRon.Capstone: hpins (`decode_embedded`; `--pins`/`--no-pins` are
   636      // outside the theorems)
   637      let pins = match con_ron::driver::pins_for_run(&a.pins, a.no_pins) {
   638          Ok(p) => p,
   639          Err(e) => {
   640              eprintln!("con-ron: {}", e);
   641              return 3;
   642          }
   643      };
   644      // What the parse line reports, printed once the index is built.
   645      hb.file_records = file_records;
   646      hb.synthesised = prepared.synthesised;
   647      // **THE STARTUP PIN WALK** (DESIGN.md §8.6 P2d, task #97-P4d): every
   648      // pinned datum the checker compares a stream record against — the six
   649      // basis blocks in both forms, the axiom pins, the reserved names and the
   650      // `Nat`-operation variants — interned ONCE, here, while the scratch tier
   651      // is still off, so that nothing the fold compares against lives in a tier
   652      // that is about to vanish.  Its result is the fold's pin parameter.
   653      // ConRon.Capstone: h5
   654      let ipins = match checker::intern_all_pins(pers, &mut st, &pins, &a.max_nat_size) {
   655          Ok(p) => p,
   656          Err(e) => return frontend_exit(&e, mode_tag),
   657      };
   658      // ONE driver, and the heartbeat is printed between its steps
   659      // (`driver::check_decls_driver`: the index, the frozen tier, and the pool
   660      // for the check phase).
   661      let jobs: u64 = match a.jobs {
   662          Some(n) => n,
   663          None => con_ron::driver::default_jobs(),
   664      };
   665      // ONE lane, whatever the flags: the driver is what builds and freezes the
   666      // index and the check phase is the pool at every worker count, so a run
   667      // with no heartbeat is the same computation as a run with one.

== crates/con-ron-core/src/arena/pins.rs#L1-L60
     1  //! `arena::pins` — the reserved names, interned ONCE (task #97-P6-4a).
     2  //!
     3  //! con-leche compares its reserved names — `natName`, `natZeroName`,
     4  //! `natSuccName`, the sixteen `Nat`-operation names, the `Bool` trio, the
     5  //! `String`/`List`/`Char` family, the standard and the trusted axiom names —
     6  //! as `Name` VALUES, which Lean builds once per nullary `def` and caches.
     7  //! The arena compares them as HANDLES, so `arena::core::pin` turned each one
     8  //! into `intern_name` of a freshly built `Name`: a `code_points` allocation
     9  //! and an `Arc<NameNode>` per path segment, then one cons-table probe per
    10  //! segment, every time.  Task #97-P6-1's counter measured what that costs on
    11  //! `Init`: **140 083 646 `NStore::intern` calls, of which 88 854 033 are
    12  //! probes of a `str` node built purely to be compared and dropped** — tens of
    13  //! millions of rebuilds of about forty constants, in `natLitSupported`'s
    14  //! three probes per literal, in `natOpNames`, in `strLitToConstructor`.
    15  //!
    16  //! This module is DESIGN.md's answer, flagged at task #97c ("the `Pins`
    17  //! record that is NOT here") and deferred there for want of a number: one
    18  //! record, filled once at the driver by `intern_reserved_pins`, and every
    19  //! `pin` of a constant name becomes a field read.
    20  //!
    21  //! **Not `arena::checker`'s `intern_all_pins`.**  That one walks the `--pins`
    22  //! RECEIPT file (the trusted pin list) into the persistent tier; this one
    23  //! interns the checker's own reserved constants.  The two run at the same
    24  //! point of the pipeline and mean different things, which is why they have
    25  //! different names.
    26  //!
    27  //! ## The table is a `Vec`, and that is what kills task #97c's hazard
    28  //!
    29  //! Task #97c declined the record because of an initialisation-order hazard:
    30  //! "a pin read before it is filled compares against the zero word and
    31  //! silently says *not `Nat`*".  A record of handle FIELDS has that hazard,
    32  //! because every 32-bit word is a syntactically valid handle.  A `Vec<NIdx>`
    33  //! does not: before `intern_reserved_pins` runs the table is EMPTY, so `pin_at`
    34  //! takes its bounds branch and raises `CheckError::Internal` — a loud stop,
    35  //! never a quiet wrong answer.  The cost is one `len` compare per read,
    36  //! against an interning walk it replaces.
    37  //!
    38  //! ## What is pinned
    39  //!
    40  //! The fifty-two names below and `basis_names::reserved_basis_names()`'s
    41  //! sixteen, plus the three interned values every `pin` site around them
    42  //! needs: the empty universe-argument list, the level `0` and the expression
    43  //! `Sort 1` (`arena::core`'s `empty_levels`, `zero_level` and `sort_one`,
    44  //! which now read this record instead of interning).
    45  //!
    46  //! All of them go into the PERSISTENT tier, because `intern_reserved_pins` runs
    47  //! before the parse, while the scratch tier is closed.  That matters twice:
    48  //! a pinned handle must survive every `drop_scratch` (it is read across all
    49  //! of them), and task #97-P6-1's `pers_find_maybe` rests on "a persistent
    50  //! node's children are persistent", which the bottom-up intern of a closed
    51  //! scratch tier gives for free.
    52  //!
    53  //! **Denotation unchanged.**  A pin is `intern_name` of the same `Name`, so
    54  //! the handle this record holds is the handle `pin` computed before —
    55  //! `denoteN` is injective and `intern` is idempotent, so pre-interning a name
    56  //! the export also carries hands the export's parse the very same handle.
    57  //! What changes is only WHEN the intern happens, and how many times.
    58  //!
    59  //! Lean twin: `proof/ConRon/Arena/Monad.lean:118-135 AState` (DESIGN.md §8.6's
    60  //! twin ledger, task #97-P6-4a) — `AState` gains a `pins : Pins` field and

== crates/con-ron-core/src/frontend/prepare.rs#L1-L50
     1  //! `proof/ConRon/Arena/Frontend/Prepare.lean` — **what happens between the
     2  //! file and the fold** (task #97 P4e part 1).
     3  //!
     4  //! `prepare_prelude` is total — no record of the stream is dropped, rewritten
     5  //! or retagged — and it does two things:
     6  //!
     7  //! 1. **the prelude's declarations first**, the stream's OWN copy of each
     8  //!    where the stream has one and a synthesised one only where it has none,
     9  //!    so a stream that declares the toolchain's `Bool` is checked on its own
    10  //!    `Bool` record;
    11  //! 2. **the ground hoist**: a pinned `Nat` operation's stream-certified
    12  //!    structural ground is moved ahead of it when the stream declares it
    13  //!    later.
    14  //!
    15  //! Moving a record earlier can only reject, never accept, which is why the
    16  //! spec con-leche proves is as simple as it is:
    17  //!
    18  //! ```text
    19  //! ∃ extra, (∀ d ∈ extra, d ∈ prelude) ∧
    20  //!   (preparePrelude ds).toList.Perm (ds.toList ++ extra)
    21  //! ```
    22  //!
    23  //! **Step 2 is `frontend::nat_op_ground`'s**, a module of its own exactly as
    24  //! con-leche's is (task #97-P4d; task #97-P4e part 1 shipped an identity
    25  //! placeholder here, because the pass needs the kernel's
    26  //! `natOpNames`/`natDivModNames`, which arrived with the pins).  It is why
    27  //! `prepare_d` takes the whole `AState` where everything else in this module
    28  //! needs only the store.
    29  //!
    30  //! **Where the store comes from.**  Only `prelude_key`, whose `.anonymous`
    31  //! fall-through has to be INTERNED, and the two functions that call it;
    32  //! [`pick_idx`] and [`declares`] are pure, exactly as con-leche's are, because
    33  //! `env::i_declaration_names` is.
    34  //! Nothing in this module reads or writes a term.
    35  //!
    36  //! **The deviation of the port into the verified core** (task #84), kept
    37  //! verbatim from `con_ron_core::frontend::prepare`: con-leche's `pick` ERASES
    38  //! the picked record from the array (`Array.eraseIdxIfInBounds`) and `frontOf`
    39  //! moves it to the front.  The Aeneas subset has no operation that takes an
    40  //! element out of a `Vec` — no `remove`, no `pop`, no `into_iter` — so the
    41  //! port splits the two halves that con-leche fuses: [`pick_idx`] is the cited
    42  //! `ds.findIdx (declares n)` with the erasure recorded in a `picked` mask
    43  //! instead of performed, [`front_of`] runs that over the prelude, and
    44  //! [`prepared_stream`] materialises the whole prepared list in ONE pass.  The
    45  //! list that comes out is the same list; the cost is one record copy per
    46  //! record, where the copied fields are handles and `Vec` spines and not terms.
    47  //! con-leche's `pickSpec`/`frontSpec` are not ported (they are `cons`-list
    48  //! specifications with no caller on the run path); `pick_spec` lives in this
    49  //! module's tests, where it still checks `pick_idx` against the specification
    50  //! on every `cargo test`.

   169  /// con-leche: ConLeche/Kernel/Basis.lean:39-45 BasisKind.decls
   170  /// Lean twin: `proof/ConRon/Arena/Checker.lean:130-168 internAllPins` — **the
   171  /// one-time tree walk of DESIGN.md §8.6 P2d**: every datum the checker compares
   172  /// a stream record against, interned into the tier that is live at the call —
   173  /// which, at the driver's call, is the persistent one.
   174  ///
   175  /// The five basis blocks' pins (what a basis block's and a quotient record's
   176  /// job compares the record with), the standard and compiler-trust axiom pins, the reserved names
   177  /// the guards compare by handle, and the `Nat`-operation pin variants, whose
   178  /// interned form is the checker's pin-list parameter (con-leche's task #304).
   179  /// First, the run's maximum `Nat` size goes into the pin record
   180  /// (`Pins::max_nat_size`): con-leche threads it beside the pin list
   181  /// (`checkDecls mode pins maxNatSize`) into every declaration's fresh state
   182  /// (`{ maxNatSize := maxNatSize }`, `Cached.declStep`, `Cached.recordJob`); here
   183  /// every worker copies it with the pins (`worker_state`) and no job writes it.
   184  /// It is stored normalised (`nat::norm`), whatever limbs the caller hands in,
   185  /// so every comparison against it reads it as the number it denotes.
   186  pub fn intern_all_pins(
   187      pers: &PersTier,
   188      st: &mut AState,
   189      pins: &Vec<NatOpPinSet>,
   190      max_nat_size: &Nat,
   191  ) -> Result<Vec<INatOpPinSet>, CheckError> {
   192      st.pins.max_nat_size = nat::norm(nat::clone(max_nat_size).limbs);
   193      match intern_all_basis(pers, st, 0) {
   194          Err(e) => Err(e),
   195          Ok(()) => match intern_all_axiom_pins(pers, st) {
   196              Err(e) => Err(e),
   197              Ok(()) => match intern_all_names(st) {
   198                  Err(e) => Err(e),
   199                  Ok(()) => intern_pin_sets(pers, st, pins, 0, Vec::new()),
   200              },
   201          },

== crates/con-ron/src/driver.rs#L1003-L1044
  1003  // the reads have no model here, and a theorem about the file is a theorem
  1004  // about its bytes.  con-leche's reads go through a handle too (its `CheckerIO`
  1005  // class's `openRead` and `read`), up to the size it read first; these go to the
  1006  // first empty read, and there is no class.
  1007  // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
  1008  
  1009  /// con-leche: ConLeche/Frontend/CheckerIO.lean:205-215 foldChunks
  1010  /// **The file handle as the parse's `ChunkSource`**: each `next_chunk` is one
  1011  /// `read_up_to` of `chunk` bytes, strictly forward, handed over whole; the
  1012  /// first empty read is the end of the input.  A failed read ends the input
  1013  /// the same way and is KEPT here, and `parse_export_handle_d` reports it in
  1014  /// place of whatever the parse of the truncated input said — so a read error
  1015  /// is exit 3, never a verdict, as before the loop moved.
  1016  pub struct HandleSource<'a, R: Read> {

  1018      pub h: &'a mut R,
  1019      /// The buffer size, `export_c::CHUNK_SIZE` in the binary.
  1020      pub chunk: usize,
  1021      /// The nonempty buffers handed out so far, for the heartbeat.
  1022      pub chunks: u64,
  1023      /// The first read failure, if any.
  1024      pub err: Option<std::io::Error>,
  1025  }

  1030      /// One read of up to `chunk` bytes; empty at the end or on a failure.
  1031      fn next_chunk(&mut self) -> Vec<u8> {
  1032          if self.err.is_some() {
  1033              return Vec::new();
  1034          }

  1037              Ok(n) => {
  1038                  buf.truncate(n);
  1039                  if n > 0 {
  1040                      self.chunks += 1;
  1041                  }
  1042                  buf
  1043              }
  1044              Err(e) => {

   586  /// con-leche: ConLeche/Driver/CheckMain.lean:233-385 checkMainG
   587  /// con-leche: ConLeche/Driver/CheckMain.lean:154-177 checkOleansG
   588  /// `check_decls_driver` with a worker state of the caller's beside each
   589  /// worker's `AState` (`init_x`, one per worker) and the caller's job: an
   590  /// `--olean` run's workers keep the module region they read a theorem's value
   591  /// from (`olean_job`, con-leche's `OleanWorker`), every other run's job is
   592  /// `checker::run_job` with nothing beside it.  The cited `checkOleansG`'s
   593  /// `start`, `alone` and `seed` (a module's worker) are at their defaults on
   594  /// this path: every record from 0, the process's one phase, an empty region.
   595  pub fn check_decls_driver_with<O, X, I, J>(
   596      pers: &PersTier,
   597      st: &mut AState,
   598      ds: &Vec<IDeclaration>,
   599      jobs: u64,
   600      obs: &mut O,
   601      init_x: I,
   602      job: J,
   603  ) -> Result<IStreamIndex, (CheckError, u64)>
   604  where
   605      O: PhaseObserver + Send,
   606      I: Fn() -> X + Sync,
   607      J: Fn(&PersTier, &mut AState, &mut X, u64) -> Result<(), (CheckError, u64)> + Sync,
   608  {
   609      // THE INDEX (the last step of the parse phase): every record's constants and
   610      // tables, a name's first entry winning, read off the records alone.
   611      obs.index_starts();
   612      let ix: IStreamIndex = stream_index::build_index(pers, st, stream_index::stream_index_empty(), ds, 0)?;
   613      obs.parse_done(pers, &st.store, ds.len());
   614      let m = ds.len();
   615      let workers = workers_for(jobs, m);
   616      obs.check_starts(m, workers);
   617      // THE BOUNDARY: the persistent tier and the index leave the state and become
   618      // a value every worker reads.  `st` keeps its (empty) store, its tables
   619      // moved out, so the observer can still read a label back through the tier.
   620      let tier: PersTier = checker::freeze_tier(&mut st.store, ix);
   621      // THE CHECK PHASE: the job at every record, on `workers` threads, each
   622      // folding it over the jobs it claims on ONE `worker_state` — the verdict and
   623      // the record a rejection names are the one-worker walk's at every `--jobs`.
   624      let heartbeat = obs.wants_check_lines();
   625      let lock: Mutex<(usize, &mut O)> = Mutex::new((0, obs));
   626      let r = parallel_all(
   627          m,
   628          workers,
   629          || (checker::worker_state(&st.pins), init_x()),
   630          |w: &mut (AState, X), k| job(&tier, &mut w.0, &mut w.1, k as u64),
   631          |w: &(AState, X), k| check_line(heartbeat, &lock, &tier, &w.0, m, ds, k),
   632      );
   633      let obs: &mut O = match lock.into_inner() {
   634          Ok((_, o)) => o,
   635          Err(e) => e.into_inner().1,
   636      };
   637      // AND THE TIER GOES BACK.  Everything after the check — the verdict line's
   638      // declaration label, the failing record's name — reads a handle back out of
   639      // `st`, and a state left frozen over a tier that has gone out of scope
   640      // answers `None` to every one of them.
   641      let ix: IStreamIndex = checker::thaw_tier(&mut st.store, tier);
   642      let v = pool_verdict(r);
   643      obs.check_done(m, match &v {

== crates/con-ron/src/pool.rs#L35-L48
    35  //! ## What a worker is, in the check phase
    36  //!
    37  //! §8.3 has said since P1 what the check phase is: "the persistent tier is
    38  //! immutable, each worker owns a scratch tier — **no atomics anywhere**"
    39  //! (`record_job` is the bracket; nothing writes the persistent tier after the
    40  //! index is built and frozen, and a worker never holds it `&mut`).  So the
    41  //! driver's `init`
    42  //! builds `checker::worker_state(pins)` — an EMPTY store, FROZEN
    43  //! (`EStore::empty_frozen`: every append a scratch append), its own `Memos`
    44  //! and `Caches`, and a COPY of
    45  //! the driver's `Pins` — and its `step` borrows the frozen `&PersTier`, which
    46  //! holds the stream's index.  A job reads it through an empty layer of its own
    47  //! at its record's view and pushes into that layer.  So a worker costs no
    48  //! environment copy at all.

   123  /// Lean twin: `proof/ConRon/Arena/Checker.lean:65-73 AState.worker` — the twin's

   125  /// **A worker's start state** (the cited `init`): the empty store, FROZEN

   127  /// to the `PersTier` the boundary froze and every append is a scratch append;

   129  /// among them (con-leche's `checkPool mode maxNatSize`, which hands it to every
   130  /// job's fresh state through `runAt` and `recordJob`).  The store stays frozen for
   131  /// the worker's life: `record_job` only empties its scratch tier.  A run with a solution builds the same state: the solution is handed to every

   134      let mut st = AState::init(EStore::empty_frozen());
   135      st.pins = pins_dup(pins);

== crates/con-ron/src/pool.rs#L233-L294
   233  
   234  /// con-leche: ConLeche/Frontend/CheckerIO.lean:486-512 parMapWorkersIO
   235  /// con-leche: ConLeche/Driver/CheckPool.lean:211-239 checkPool
   236  /// **`step` at every index of `0..n`, on a pool of `workers` threads** — the
   237  /// module note's trusted claim is this function's contract:
   238  ///
   239  /// > If it returns `Ok(())`, every index in `0..n` was claimed by some worker,
   240  /// > each worker built its state with `init()` once and folded `step` over its
   241  /// > claimed indices in claim order, which is increasing, and every step
   242  /// > returned `Ok(())`.
   243  ///
   244  /// On a failure it returns the LEAST failing index with its error
   245  /// (`ParallelError::Step`), whatever the timing.  `after(&st, k)` runs on the
   246  /// worker's thread after each step it made, with the worker's state by `&`
   247  /// (the driver's heartbeat); it cannot change an outcome.
   248  ///
   249  /// The workers are `std::thread::scope`d, with `STACK_BYTES` of stack each.
   250  /// `workers` is the count the caller has already clamped
   251  /// (`driver::workers_for`: `max(1, min(jobs, n))`); if the OS refuses to
   252  /// spawn one, the pool runs on those it has, and on the calling thread if it
   253  /// has none — the contract holds at every worker count, so the answer does
   254  /// not depend on it.
   255  pub fn parallel_all<S, E: Send>(
   256      n: usize,
   257      workers: usize,
   258      init: impl Fn() -> S + Sync,
   259      step: impl Fn(&mut S, usize) -> Result<(), E> + Sync,
   260      after: impl Fn(&S, usize) + Sync,
   261  ) -> Result<(), ParallelError<E>> {
   262      let next = AtomicUsize::new(0);
   263      let limit = AtomicUsize::new(n);
   264      let run = || worker(n, &next, &limit, &init, &step, &after);
   265      let mut results: Vec<Vec<(usize, Result<(), E>)>> = Vec::with_capacity(workers);
   266      let mut panicked = false;
   267      std::thread::scope(|scope| {
   268          let mut handles = Vec::with_capacity(workers);
   269          for w in 0..workers {
   270              let spawned = std::thread::Builder::new()
   271                  .stack_size(STACK_BYTES)
   272                  .name(format!("check-{}", w))
   273                  .spawn_scoped(scope, &run);
   274              match spawned {
   275                  Ok(h) => handles.push(h),
   276                  // Out of threads, or out of address space for another stack:
   277                  // run on the workers already spawned (the module note).
   278                  Err(_) => break,
   279              }
   280          }
   281          if handles.is_empty() {
   282              results.push(run());
   283          }
   284          for h in handles {
   285              match h.join() {
   286                  Ok(rs) => results.push(rs),
   287                  Err(_) => panicked = true,
   288              }
   289          }
   290      });
   291      if panicked {
   292          return Err(ParallelError::Panicked);
   293      }
   294      first_failure(merge_results(n, results))

   155  /// check — is a **decline**, exit 2, the same code as "not implemented",
   156  /// because that is what it is: the port cannot carry this input, and says so
   157  /// rather than rejecting the stream (1) or claiming a checker bug (3).
   158  pub fn exit_code(e: &CheckError) -> u8 {
   159      match e {

   161          CheckError::Invalid(_) => 1,
   162          CheckError::Internal(_) => 3,
   163          CheckError::Native(_) => 2,
   164      }

== proof/ConRon/Arena/Denote.lean#L185-L208
   185  /-- con-leche: ConLeche/Kernel/Expr.lean:369-488 Expr — the fuel-indexed
   186  readback of an expression handle. -/
   187  def denoteEAux (st : EStore) : Nat → EIdx → Option Expr
   188    | 0, _ => none
   189    | f + 1, i =>
   190      (st.view i).bind fun v =>
   191        match v with
   192        | .bvar k => some (.bvar k)
   193        | .fvar k ty => (denoteEAux st f ty).map (Expr.fvar k)
   194        | .sort u => (denoteL st.ls u).map Expr.sort
   195        | .const n us => opt2 Expr.const (denoteN st.ns n) (denoteLs st.lss us)
   196        | .app g a => opt2 Expr.app (denoteEAux st f g) (denoteEAux st f a)
   197        | .lam ty b => opt2 Expr.lam (denoteEAux st f ty) (denoteEAux st f b)
   198        | .forallE ty b => opt2 Expr.forallE (denoteEAux st f ty) (denoteEAux st f b)
   199        | .letE ty w b =>
   200          opt3 Expr.letE (denoteEAux st f ty) (denoteEAux st f w) (denoteEAux st f b)
   201        | .lit l => some (.lit l)
   202        | .proj n k e =>
   203          opt2 (fun nm x => Expr.proj nm k x) (denoteN st.ns n) (denoteEAux st f e)
   204

   206  expression handle, at the store's own node count as fuel. -/
   207  def denoteE (st : EStore) (i : EIdx) : Option Expr :=
   208    denoteEAux st (st.nodeCount + 1) i

== proof/ConRon/Arena/WF.lean#L1-L39
     1  /-
     2  # Store well-formedness and the store layer's theorems (DESIGN.md §8.3, P2a)
     3  
     4  `StoreWF` is the arena's own invariant — con-leche's `TWF`
     5  (`Setlec/Kernel/ArenaWF.lean:900`, 28 clauses) redrawn for the
     6  per-constructor, high-tag representation.  It lives here, beside the
     7  implementation, importing nothing from `ConRon.Refine`: con-leche's lesson 27,
     8  "implementation may import a *self-contained* data-structure verification".
     9  
    10  Each store's invariant is `∃ rank, …WFAt st rank`.  The rank is existential
    11  because nothing at runtime stores it (DESIGN §8.3: "zero runtime cost, and no
    12  global array order is needed with per-constructor arrays"); what it buys is
    13  
    14  * **acyclicity**, hence a terminating `denote`;
    15  * **a fuel bound**: a persistent node's rank is below the persistent node
    16    count and a scratch node's below the total, so `nodeCount + 1` — the fuel
    17    `denoteE` uses — is always enough, and `dropScratch` shrinks both sides of
    18    the persistent clause together.
    19  
    20  The clauses, in the order a reader meets them:
    21  
    22  | clause | what it says |
    23  |---|---|
    24  | `childOK` | every child is in range, ranked below its parent, and persistent if the parent is |
    25  | `rankP` / `rankS` | ranks are below the tier's node count (the fuel bound) |
    26  | `consP` / `consS` | each tier's cons table is exactly the inverse of that tier's `get` |
    27  | `fresh` | a scratch cons entry never duplicates a persistent one (DESIGN §8.3's cross-tier canonicity; con-leche's `t_cons_fresh`) |
    28  | `derExact` | the derived column is `derOfView` of the node — *locally*; the global `derived st i = e.data` is a theorem (`derived_exact`) |
    29  | `sized` | the derived array is as long as the node array |
    30  | `cap` | no constructor array exceeds its handle shape's index range (2^30 for `app`, 2^26 for the rest), so the index is injective on it |
    31  | `scrOff` | the scratch tier is empty while the scratch flag is off |
    32  | `sync` | the nesting's scratch flags move together (task #97a) |
    33  
    34  `childOK`'s third conjunct — *persistent parents have persistent children* —
    35  is what makes `dropScratch` sound: without it a persistent node could point
    36  into a tier that is about to vanish.  It needs no hypothesis at `intern`,
    37  because `scrOff` makes a scratch handle undecodable while the flag is off, so
    38  a valid child of a node appended to the persistent tier is persistent already.
    39  -/

== proof/ConRon/Bridge/Specs.lean#L1-L31
     1  /-
     2  # `ConRon.Bridge.Specs` — one `@[spec]` theorem per `Monad.lean` primitive
     3  
     4  **One spec theorem per (B) primitive, in one shape**, so that the
     5  verification-condition generator (`vcgen`, on native `Std.WP` triples) can
     6  walk a twin's body without any store reasoning appearing in the proof text.
     7  The shape is the seven-rule template (DESIGN §8.6, `P2s SPIKE`, and task
     8  #97s's section):
     9  
    10  ```lean
    11  @[spec] theorem f_spec (s₀ : AState) (args…) (pre…) :
    12      ⦃fun s => s = s₀⦄ f args ⦃fun r s' => Post s₀ r s'; ⊤⦄
    13  ```
    14  
    15  1. **the precondition is `s = s₀` and nothing else** — every real
    16     precondition is an ordinary hypothesis of the theorem, so `vcgen` turns it
    17     into a side goal instead of an entailment to discharge in the logic;
    18  2. **exception postcondition `⊤` (partial correctness), never the default
    19     `⊥`** (`⦃P⦄ x ⦃Q⦄` is TOTAL correctness in `Std.WP`) — a (B) function may
    20     fail and Theorem 1 claims nothing then (con-leche's `SimAt`,
    21     `Verify/SimI.lean:244`);
    22  3. **the postcondition names `s₀`**, the only way to state
    23     `Ext s₀.store s'.store` in a triple;
    24  4. **"the subject denotes" is an `isSome`, never a named `Expr`**;
    25  5. **the answer is a named relation or predicate** (`Rel.lean`'s `RelE`
    26     family, `Grind.lean`'s `Ans`/`MapRel`), never a bare `∀ e, … → …`;
    27  6. **a memo insert's spec states that the INVARIANT is preserved**, not that
    28     the table grew — the rule that matters most;
    29  7. **one named failure primitive** (`fail`): every failure site goes
    30     through it, so one spec covers them all and the Rust has one function to
    31     match.

== proof/ConRon/Bridge/Inductives/Run.lean#L60-L76
    60  /-- con-leche: ConLeche/Verify/SimI.lean:244 SimAt — **the PURE grade's
    61  statement**: from a well-formed store, an ACCEPTING run of the twin returns an
    62  answer related to the pure side's by `R`, having only grown the arena.
    63  
    64  Partial correctness, as everywhere in this library: a (B) function may fail
    65  and Theorem 1 claims nothing then — which is why the hypothesis is
    66  `c s0 = .ok (r, s')` and not an unconditional equation.
    67  
    68  **RUN form rather than a Hoare triple** (DESIGN `### Task #97-P3-Checker`
    69  §1): this tier's work is composition, inversion and list induction rather
    70  than verification conditions, and the checker tier that consumes `IndSpec`
    71  (`Bridge/Checker/Arms.lean`) is written in run form too (`AM.bind_ok` is its
    72  inversion). -/
    73  @[expose] def PSpec {α : Type} (P : EStore → Prop) (c : AM α) (R : EStore → α → Prop) :
    74      Prop :=
    75    ∀ (s₀ s' : AState) (r : α), StateOK s₀ → P s₀.store → c s₀ = .ok (r, s') →
    76      PStep s₀ s' ∧ R s'.store r

== proof/ConRon/Bridge/Inductives/Rel.lean#L61-L78
    61  /-! ## The core grade -/
    62  
    63  /-- con-leche: none — **the bridge between the two grades**: a pure step
    64  preserves the whole checking invariant, by `Bridge/StateOK.lean`'s
    65  `CheckOK.mono`.  This is what lets a core-grade function call a pure-grade one
    66  and keep its own hypothesis. -/
    67  theorem PStep.toCore {env : Env} {fe : IFEnv} {s s' : AState}
    68      (h : PStep s s') (hc : CheckOK false env fe s) : CoreStep env fe s s' :=
    69    ⟨hc.monoF h.ok h.ext h.cframe h.pins, h.ext, h.pins⟩

    72  statement**: the same at a function that calls the knot, so the invariant is
    73  `CheckOK` and the frame is `CoreStep`.  The pure side's fuel existential lives
    74  inside `R`, as `Bridge/Core/Knot.lean`'s `SimE` has it. -/

    76      (P : EStore → Prop) (c : AM α) (R : EStore → α → Prop) : Prop :=

    78      c s₀ = .ok (r, s') → CoreStep env fe s₀ s' ∧ R s'.store r

== proof/ConRon/Bridge/Inductives/StructParts.lean#L128-L174
   128  /-! ## The spines -/
   129  
   130  /-- con-leche: ConLeche/Kernel/Inductives/StructParts.lean:52-53 structPsAt
   131  The parameter variables as seen from under `o` extra binders.
   132  
   133  **Proof:** a `Nat` recursion over
   134  `internBVarE_run` with the cursor `k` generalised.  The pure side is a
   135  `List.range` map, so the step is `List.range_succ_eq_map` and one `omega` on
   136  the index arithmetic (`k + (j + 1) = k + 1 + j`). -/
   137  theorem structPsAt_go_run (o nP : Nat) : ∀ (n k : Nat) {s s' : AState}
   138      {r : List EIdx}, StateOK s → Arena.structPsAt.go o nP n k s = .ok (r, s') →
   139      PStep s s' ∧ Frontend.denoteEList s'.store r
   140        = some ((List.range n).map fun j => Expr.bvar (o + nP - 1 - (k + j))) := by
   141    intro n
   142    induction n with
   143    | zero =>
   144      intro k s s' r hok hrun
   145      simp only [Arena.structPsAt.go] at hrun
   146      obtain ⟨rfl, rfl⟩ := AM.pure_ok hrun
   147      exact ⟨PStep.refl hok, rfl⟩
   148    | succ n ih =>
   149      intro k s s' r hok hrun
   150      simp only [Arena.structPsAt.go] at hrun
   151      obtain ⟨b, s₁, h1, h2⟩ := AM.bind_ok hrun
   152      obtain ⟨rest, s₂, h3, h4⟩ := AM.bind_ok h2
   153      obtain ⟨hstep1, hb⟩ := internBVarE_run hok h1
   154      obtain ⟨hstep2, hrest⟩ := ih (k + 1) hstep1.ok h3
   155      obtain ⟨rfl, rfl⟩ := AM.pure_ok h4
   156      refine ⟨hstep1.trans hstep2, ?_⟩
   157      have hkey : ((List.range (n + 1)).map fun j => Expr.bvar (o + nP - 1 - (k + j)))
   158          = Expr.bvar (o + nP - 1 - k) ::
   159            ((List.range n).map fun j => Expr.bvar (o + nP - 1 - (k + 1 + j))) := by
   160        rw [List.range_succ_eq_map, List.map_cons, List.map_map]
   161        congr 1
   162        refine List.map_congr_left (fun j _ => ?_)
   163        simp only [Function.comp_apply]
   164        congr 1
   165        omega
   166      rw [hkey]
   167      simp only [Frontend.denoteEList, denote_ext hb hstep2.ext, hrest]
   168  
   169  theorem structPsAt_spec (o nP : Nat) :
   170      PSpec PT (Arena.structPsAt o nP) (REL (ConLeche.structPsAt o nP)) := by
   171    intro s₀ s' r hok _ hrun
   172    obtain ⟨hstep, hd⟩ := structPsAt_go_run o nP nP 0 hok hrun
   173    refine ⟨hstep, ?_⟩
   174    simpa only [ConLeche.structPsAt, Nat.zero_add] using hd

    68      ∀ f {eager : Bool}, KnotSpec eager env fe f

== proof/ConRon/Refine2/Tactic/Lockstep.lean#L1-L30
     1  /-
     2  # `ConRon.Refine2.Tactic.Lockstep` — the lockstep judgement and the `lockstep` tactic
     3  
     4  Task #97-T2-TACTIC.  Theorem 2 in its lockstep shape (task #97-T2-AUDIT §6)
     5  relates two programs doing the same operations in the same order, over a
     6  state relation that says only "the same data in two representations".  So a
     7  proof of one `_refines` lemma is a ZIP of two do-blocks: peel one bind on each
     8  side, close the correspondence of the two callees with a registered lemma,
     9  continue with the related results.  This file makes that zip a tactic.
    10  
    11  ## The judgement
    12  
    13  `LS pers R m lst x` — *every outcome of the Rust computation `m` is matched by
    14  the twin action `x` run from `lst`*: an `Ok a` by an `ok (b, lst')` with
    15  `R a b` in a related post-state, an `Err e` by the twin throwing at the same
    16  kind (`AErrSim`).  It is `Sim₀` with a relation for the answer instead of an
    17  abstraction function, and with the Rust equation moved into the judgement, so
    18  that the Rust program is visible in the GOAL beside the twin (`LS.toSim₀` is the
    19  bridge back).  Four companion judgements carry the other Rust callee shapes:
    20  
    21  | judgement | Rust callee shape | example |
    22  |---|---|---|
    23  | `LS`  | `Result (Result α CheckError × AState)` — state threaded | `intern_e_app`, a recursive call |
    24  | `LSR` | `Result (Result α CheckError)` — reads, may fail | `view` |
    25  | `LSV` | `Result α` — reads, total | `lift_get`, `inst_list_cutoff` |
    26  | `LSW` | `Result AState` — writes, total | `lift_set` |
    27  | `LSP` | `Result α`, **Rust only** — no twin counterpart | `fuel - 1#u64`, `dup2`, `eidx_nat_key`, `fail` |
    28  | `LSM` | `Result (Result α × AState × M)` — a memoised walk, memo beside the result | `consts_resolve_f_go`, `intern_expr_go` |
    29  | `LSRM` | `Result (Result α × M)` — a memoised reader walk | `all_level_params_defined_go` |
    30  

== proof/ConRon/Refine2/Tactic/Lockstep.lean#L164-L168
   164  /-- **The lockstep judgement** for a state-threading Rust computation. -/
   165  def LS {α β : Type} (pers : arena.store.PersTier) (R : α → β → Prop)
   166      (m : Result (core.result.Result α kernel.core_types.CheckError × arena.monad.AState))
   167      (lst : AState) (x : AM β) : Prop :=
   168    ∀ o st', m = ok (o, st') → LOut pers R o st' (x.run lst)

== proof/ConRon/Refine2/Tactic/Lockstep.lean#L170-L174
   170  /-- A Rust READ that may fail: the state is `st` before and after. -/
   171  def LSR {α β : Type} (pers : arena.store.PersTier) (R : α → β → Prop)
   172      (m : Result (core.result.Result α kernel.core_types.CheckError))
   173      (st : arena.monad.AState) (lst : AState) (x : AM β) : Prop :=
   174    ∀ o, m = ok o → LOut pers R o st (x.run lst)

== proof/ConRon/Refine2/Tactic/Lockstep.lean#L633-L645
   633  /-- **The lockstep judgement of a memoised state walk**: `LS` of the walk with
   634  its memo moved into the answer; `R` relates `(answer, memo)` to the twin's
   635  answer (typically the twin's `(answer, memo)` pair). -/
   636  def LSM {α β M : Type} (pers : arena.store.PersTier) (R : α × M → β → Prop)
   637      (m : Result (core.result.Result α kernel.core_types.CheckError × arena.monad.AState × M))
   638      (lst : AState) (x : AM β) : Prop :=
   639    LS pers R (packM m) lst x
   640  
   641  /-- **The lockstep judgement of a memoised reader walk** at the state `st`. -/
   642  def LSRM {α β M : Type} (pers : arena.store.PersTier) (R : α × M → β → Prop)
   643      (m : Result (core.result.Result α kernel.core_types.CheckError × M))
   644      (st : arena.monad.AState) (lst : AState) (x : AM β) : Prop :=
   645    LS pers R (packRM st m) lst x

  2662  macro "lockstep" : tactic => `(tactic| repeat' lockstep_step)
